ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 35% high-intensity (white) pixels primarily located on the distal margins of the lobes, versus 65% low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels dominating the central, basal, and medial regions.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-contrast white pigmentation is concentrated on the lateral extremities of both lobes. The left lobe contains a large contiguous white region with irregular interior black spotting. The right lobe shows a more fragmented, speckled distribution of white pixels against a black base. The center and lower fluke regions are uniformly low-intensity black.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: A deep, narrow U-shaped central depression; the interior angle is approximately 40-45 degrees, though the exact apex is slightly obscured by the orientation of the fluke relative to the water surface.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: The trailing edge exhibits high-frequency, irregular serrations across the entire visible margin. Significant pixel-level indentations and peaks create a jagged boundary, particularly prominent on the inner half of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge follows a sigmoidal curve, beginning with a convex bulge near the median notch and transitioning into a concave sweep toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Highly localized clusters of circular, elevated, high-contrast tan and white pixel groups (barnacles) are visible at the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: The distal tips of both lobes show significant protrusion and irregularity due to heavy barnacle colonization, which alters the expected smooth geometric contour of the fluke tips.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'ink-blot' style pigmentation on the left lobe, where isolated black pixel clusters are fully encapsulated within a white field.
